task_payload.symptom: A callable instance used as a custom Click option type crashes during command construction with AttributeError because the object has no __name__ attribute.
must_answer: why it is not a parser/runtime invocation issue

uv run pytest -q tests/test_m1nd_seeded_callable_type.py (pre-fix failure capture)
task_results.notes: The crash occurs before argument parsing or command invocation: `click.option()` constructs an `Option`, which constructs a `Parameter`, which calls `types.convert_type()` during decoration.
evidence: src/click/decorators.py:373-375 instantiates `Option` inside the decorator, so failure happens during command construction rather than at runtime.
src/click/core.py:2179-2183 calls `types.convert_type(type, default)` inside `Parameter.__init__` before parsing or invocation.

src/click/types.py:1218-1259 falls through to `FuncParamType` for generic callable types, and src/click/types.py:185-188 reads `func.__name__`, which callable instances like `UpperCase()` do not define.

Pre-fix `uv run pytest -q tests/test_m1nd_seeded_callable_type.py` failed with `AttributeError` at src/click/types.py:187; the next focused regression check is that seeded test plus tests/test_types.py::test_func_param_type_uses_value_error_message.

task_payload.claim: README/docs say Click supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime.

tests_or_commands_run: probe_m1nd.py run [ingest,search(lazy loading)] on click shared fixture
nl -ba on README.md, docs/index.rst, docs/complex.md, and src/click/core.py
task_results.notes: I do not see a hard docs drift here, but the headline claim is shorthand for a supported extension pattern rather than default `Group` behavior.
evidence: Claim sources are README.md:16-18 and docs/index.rst:21-23, both stating that Click supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime.

docs/complex.md:252-285 and 339-355 documents the supported pattern: subclass `Group`, override `get_command`, lazily import commands, and expect lazy loads during command resolution, help rendering, and shell completion.

Code truth is src/click/core.py:1806-1810 and 1935-1959: the default `Group.get_command()` only looks up `self.commands`, but both `format_commands()` and `resolve_command()` route through `get_command()`, which is exactly the extension seam the docs rely on.
Conclusion: no docs drift, with the nuance that lazy loading is a supported `Group` extension seam, not automatic behavior in the stock `Group` implementation.
